identity.question: Will the Republicans win the New York governor race in 2026?

limits: Raw release and crosstabs captured before parse (HTTP 200), hashes/clocks retained. Siena statewide likely-voter estimate distinct from Siena Oct9 NY-CD21 likely voters, Marist statewide registered voters, and Quinnipiac statewide likely voters. Different samples/modes/times; rounded toplines only; no combined estimate or forecast.

poll_facts.method: Dual-frame landline+cell phone; 652 by phone and 492 by text-to-web; English; stratified probability sample from L2 voter database; weighted to NY voter-file demographics on age, region, race/ethnicity, education, party identification, gender, and combined stated/derived vote likelihood. Open-ended answers coded by a single human coder.
poll_facts.moe: Core question sample n=1,144: +/-3.9 percentage points including design effects from weighting. Entire survey n=991: +/-4.2 points including weighting design effects; these are distinct samples/MOEs.
poll_facts.precision_limit: Crosstab is rounded percentages, no unrounded candidate counts. Choice labels are “Democrat Kathy Hochul,” “Republican Bruce Blakeman,” “Someone else,” “Don’t know/Refused”; choices rotated.
poll_facts.question: Q3. If the election for Governor was held today, who would you vote for if the candidates were:  [CHOICES ROTATED] Sample size=1,144
poll_facts.question_order: Governor vote is Q3; preceded by Q1 NY right-track and Q2 US right-track questions; next Q4 state attorney general.
poll_facts.topline: Hochul 50%, Blakeman 41%, someone else 0%, don’t know/refused 9% (published rounded percentages). Article states little changed from August: 49%–39%.
